newsitem.title: INDIA: India ruling alliance sets budget vote talks.
newsitem.headline: India ruling alliance sets budget vote talks.

text.p: India's ruling United Front alliance said on Monday it will hold talks with major political parties on April 9 to seek a way to salvage the budget for 1997/98 (April-March) from the country's political turmoil.
"The Steering Committee of the United Front is going to meet on April 9 at 5 pm (1130 GMT)," United Front spokesman Jaipal Reddy told reporters.
"We will take a collective view on the budget and after that we will get in touch with the speaker (of the lower house of parliament) and other parties and evolve consensus view."
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda faces a vote of confidence on April 11 following the decision by the Congress party, his former make-or-break ally, to withdraw support to the 10-month old government.
Most political parties have said they would not allow the political crisis to derail the budget presented by Finance Minister P.Chidambaram on February 28.
But they have offered different solutions to end the impasse, including a proposal to take up the discussion on budget after the vote of confidence.
